The key word of the hook prop is cut at the phone screen edge from 5.6 to 8.6 s (frames 168 to 258, shot 4.0 to 8.7 s, both treatments). All three lenses saw it. Cause in code: StreetHubSupport Phone starts the text at x = -w/2+90 = -20 at 25 px bold inside a screen clip that ends at x = w/2-12 = 98. That leaves about 118 px, which is too narrow for 'Flash Flood'.

B2 legibility: s4 chip-glow detail push. The camera push (scale 1 to 1.4 toward the lamp and chip midpoint, FloodStationFilm chip-glow case) carries the enclosure and its 'flood risk' bar label past the left frame edge from 24.0 to 25.2 s (frames 720 to 756). The story lens names the cut label and the picture lens saw the enclosure leave the frame.

B3 layout: the blank 'Field result' card, the object that carries the film's turn, is cut by the right frame edge. It happens at rest in the s7 validation-card detail shot (48.8 to 49.2 s after its slide-in at 48.0 to 48.8 s, frames 1440 to 1476) and in the s8 no-field-card shot (49.2 to 52.1 s, frames 1476 to 1563). proposal_assessment: A minimal renderer-only correction in video-engine/src/modern/episodes/2026-10-15/, with board text, narration, claims, mix, captions and timing unchanged, is SUFFICIENT for B1 to B5 only. It is NOT sufficient for the whole report. B1, in StreetHubSupport.tsx Phone: lay out the banner so 'Flash Flood' and 'Warning' fit inside the banner inner width with at least an 8 px margin, using widthOf to measure. Either move the warning triangle to its own row or shrink it and start the text near x = -w/2+28, or pass a larger w only in the phone-late call. Keep the rendered glyph size at least at today's 25 units times the 1.5 shot scale for phone legibility, and keep the same strings. Check both rotations (A at -10 degrees, B at 8) for every frame from 168 to 261. B2, in FloodStationFilm.tsx chip-glow: cap the detail push scale and focus so the risk bar, its 'flood risk' label and the lamp stay at least 40 px inside the left edge for every frame of the detail shot, about 23.8 to 25.4 s (frames 714 to 762). B3, in validation-card and no-field-card: shrink the result card (cs about 0.7 instead of 0.8 in no-field-card, and a matching rest scale or x in validation-card) or move it left. Its full body must fit inside the frame under the composed Cam and PlaceSubject transform, per treatment (A dollyThrough, B truckAcross), for every frame from 1440 to 1563. The R15f constraints must still hold: the 98.82% figure, its heading and 'Reported by' at least 40 px from the left edge, the tag at least 30 px, 'None reported' ending by x 1050, 'Field result' clear of the disclosure chip, all above the caption band. The stamp mark and reacher target are derived from card2 and cs, so they will follow. B4, in curb-table: move the s9-tag so it overlaps neither the bench station (about x 700 to 770, y 590 to 968) nor the case pocket. In B it must also stay inside the 1.45 Cam frame for frames 1716 to 1782. B5, in flood-paths: reduce the screen height, for example h 950, so the bezel ends at or above y 1240 for frames 1143 to 1230. B6 can't be fixed renderer-only. The 18.4 s cut and the label reveal are board shot and s3-event-3 timing. Delaying the labels to after 19.14 s would desynchronise them from their bound event and leave about 0.66 s to read four labels, which creates a new legibility failure. Rendering the optical column under the weather-row view would be a false binding. The fix needs a bounded board edit, for example extending the optical-lens shot through the clause end and dropping or relocating the weather labels, with narration, claims, mix and caption timing unchanged. B7 can't be fixed renderer-only. Moving the tag under B4 uncovers the station and reduces the fading reading, but the tuck-into-pocket and latch-shut actions are board-described s9 events. Changing their meaning needs a bounded board edit and an independent pivot review. B8 to B10 depend on board event windows and staging. Some finish items can be fixed renderer-only (the Head lid threshold, arm targets and layer order), but the pace holds and the closing answer need event or shot edits. The consolidated correction must therefore run as one standard-scope mandatory repair (comprehension plus modern-film floor) that includes the B1 to B5 renderer fixes. A technical-integrity plan is not admissible for this report, because BOUNDED_CREATIVE_RELEASE.md requires every original finding to be covered exactly once by a technical category, and B6 to B10 have none.
